questions.q: In agricultural marketing, the specific monetary value attached to a farm produce for exchange is referred to as its ________.
options: Advertisement
Demand
Subsidy
Price
questions.explain: Pricing is the process of setting a financial value on a product that consumers must pay in order to acquire it.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Animal Feeding, Fishery, Forestry & Agribusiness
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: Which of the following is a primary internal determinant of the price a farmer sets for his agricultural produce?
options: The cost of production
The name of the farmer's village
The type of car the farmer drives
The colour of the tractor
questions.explain: Cost of production (money spent on inputs, labour, and operations) is the baseline for setting prices. A farmer must set a price above this cost to make a profit.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Animal Feeding, Fishery, Forestry & Agribusiness
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: According to the economic forces of demand and supply, what generally happens to the price of a farm produce when the demand is high but the supply is very low?
options: The price falls sharply
The price rises significantly
The price remains completely unchanged
The product is given out for free
questions.explain: When many people want a product (high demand) but there is a scarcity (low supply), the scarcity allows sellers to increase the price.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Animal Feeding, Fishery, Forestry & Agribusiness
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: During the peak harvest season of maize, the markets are flooded with the crop. Consequently, the price of maize usually ________.
options: Increases to its highest point
Decreases due to surplus supply
Is dictated purely by advertising
Becomes equivalent to the cost of a tractor
questions.explain: Seasonal produce experiences price drops during harvest time because the massive surplus (high supply) gluts the market, pushing prices down.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Animal Feeding, Fishery, Forestry & Agribusiness
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: How does the 'quantity of produce' bought at once influence the price per unit offered by the seller?
options: Buying in small quantities attracts the highest possible discounts
Bulk buying often attracts a discount, reducing the price per unit
Buying in large quantities doubles the individual unit price
Quantity has no bearing on pricing whatsoever
questions.explain: Farmers and wholesalers often offer lower prices (bulk discounts) to buyers who purchase produce in very large quantities to clear their stock quickly.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Animal Feeding, Fishery, Forestry & Agribusiness
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: In determining the price of farm produce, 'quality of produce' dictates that ________.
options: Bruised and rotting fruits will sell for the exact same price as fresh ones
Premium, fresh, and well-sorted produce commands a higher market price
Lower quality produce is illegal to sell
Quality only matters for livestock, not for crops
questions.explain: Buyers are willing to pay more for products that are attractive, healthy, and of high quality, making quality a major price determinant.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Animal Feeding, Fishery, Forestry & Agribusiness
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: Market price is best described as the ________.
options: Price arbitrarily set by the government for land
Prevailing price at which goods are currently being bought and sold in an open market
Cost of transporting goods from the farm to the store
Amount paid as tax on the goods
questions.explain: The market price is the current equilibrium price agreed upon by buyers and sellers exchanging goods in the open market at any given time.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Animal Feeding, Fishery, Forestry & Agribusiness
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: The marketing strategy that involves communicating information about a farm product to the public to persuade them to buy is called ________.
options: Harvesting
Book keeping
Advertising
Packaging
questions.explain: Advertising creates awareness about the availability, quality, and price of a product with the intent of increasing its demand and sales.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Animal Feeding, Fishery, Forestry & Agribusiness
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT an effective medium for advertising agricultural produce to consumers?
options: Radio broadcasts
Handbills and posters
Hiding the products in an unmarked warehouse
Social media platforms
questions.explain: Advertising requires high visibility and communication. Hiding products keeps the public unaware, which is the exact opposite of advertising.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Animal Feeding, Fishery, Forestry & Agribusiness
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: Which of the following situations will most likely cause the price of yams to rise sharply?
options: When it is the off-season and yams are very scarce
When the government gives free yams to everyone
During a massive bumper harvest of yams across the country
When the yams are poorly stored and begin to rot
questions.explain: During the off-season, produce becomes scarce (low supply), which forces the market price to rise sharply due to steady demand.
